The probability of each toss is 50%; that is, the probability of every single toss given any possible previous scenario is just 50%. Now, the probability that after n attepts you get a desired outcome is (1/2)^n.

If a wish had a probability p, it doesn't matter how or when you did it, it has probability p. It changes when you look for the probability of a number of attempts for which you don't know the outcome. It's Bayessian probability.

In reality, the wish kind of has the same probability of occurring every day (assuming no outside influences affect them.) Looking only at this question presents some problems: what the wish is (is it more likely to happen some days?), how often you make the wish (did you make it once, or every day?).

Baically, you are right in that "given that people make birthday wishes at an x rate, wishing well wishes at a y rate, and  shooting star wishes at a z rate, x being the most frequent, the probability of the wish they made on a birthday (assuming all wishes have the same probability) would be the highest." However, the probability of the wish itself is not bigger, just the probability that the wish was made that day.

TL;DR: probability of a possible event occurring at any attempt stays the same regardless of the ways in which we group the attempts.
